sanskrit: tato 'bravīc chāṃtanavaḥ sarvān eva mahārathān eṣa bhīmo raṇe kruddho dhārtarāṣṭrān mahārathān
english: Then the son of Śaṃtanu spoke to all the great chariot-warriors: "Here is Bhīma, enraged in battle, striking down the great car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons—

sanskrit: yathāprāgryān yathājyeṣṭhān yathāśūrāṃś ca saṃgatān nipātayaty ugradhanvā taṃ pramathnīta pārthivāḥ
english: "the foremost, the eldest, and the bravest gathered together—this fierce-bowed one lays them low. Crush him, O kings!"

sanskrit: evam uktās tataḥ sarve dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikāḥ abhyadravanta saṃkruddhā bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: Thus addressed, all the soldiers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son rushed in fury upon mighty Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: bhagadattaḥ prabhinnena kuñjareṇa viśāṃ pate apatat sahasā tatra yatra bhīmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Bhagadatta, mounted on an elephant in rut, O lord of peoples, fell suddenly upon the place where Bhīma stood firm.

sanskrit: āpatann eva ca raṇe bhīmasenaṃ śilāśitaiḥ adṛśyaṃ samare cakre jīmūta iva bhāskaram
english: Even as he charged, with arrows whetted on stone he made Bhīmasena invisible in the fray, as a thundercloud hides the sun.

sanskrit: abhimanyumukhās tatra nāmṛṣyanta mahārathāḥ bhīmasyācchādanaṃ saṃkhye svabāhubalam āśritāḥ
english: The great car-warriors led by Abhimanyu, trusting in the strength of their own arms, could not endure this veiling of Bhīma in the battle.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ śaravarṣeṇa samantāt paryavārayan gajaṃ ca śaravṛṣṭyā taṃ bibhidus te samantataḥ
english: With a downpour of arrows they hemmed him in on every side, and with a rain of shafts they pierced that elephant from all directions.

sanskrit: sa śastravṛṣṭyābhihataḥ prādravad dviguṇaṃ padam prāgjyotiṣagajo rājan nānāliṅgaiḥ sutejanaiḥ
english: Struck by that storm of weapons, the elephant of Prāgjyotiṣa, O king, riddled with many keen and various-marked shafts, charged forward at redoubled pace.

sanskrit: saṃjātarudhirotpīḍaḥ prekṣaṇīyo 'bhavad raṇe gabhastibhir ivārkasya saṃsyūto jalado mahān
english: Its blood gushing forth, it became a sight to behold in the fray, like a great cloud shot through with the sun's rays.

sanskrit: sa codito madasrāvī bhagadattena vāraṇaḥ abhyadhāvata tān sarvān kālotsṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ dviguṇaṃ javam āsthāya kampayaṃś caraṇair mahīm
english: Goaded on by Bhagadatta, the elephant streaming with rut rushed upon them all like Death loosed by Time, and, gathering twofold speed, made the earth tremble beneath its feet.

sanskrit: tasya tat sumahad rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve mahārathāḥ asahyaṃ manyamānās te nātipramanaso 'bhavan
english: Beholding that enormous form, all the great car-warriors, deeming it irresistible, lost much of their cheer.

sanskrit: tatas tu nṛpatiḥ kruddho bhīmasenaṃ stanāntare ājaghāna naravyāghra śareṇa nataparvaṇā
english: Then the king, enraged, O tiger among men, struck Bhīmasena upon the breast with a smooth-jointed arrow.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsas tena rājñā mahārathaḥ mūrchayābhiparītāṅgo dhvajayaṣṭim upāśritaḥ
english: Deeply pierced by that king, the great archer and mighty car-warrior, his limbs overcome by a swoon, leaned upon his banner-staff.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu bhītān samālakṣya bhīmasenaṃ ca mūrchitam nanāda balavan nādaṃ bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān
english: Seeing them frightened and Bhīmasena fallen into a swoon, the valiant Bhagadatta let forth a mighty roar.

sanskrit: tato ghaṭotkaco rājan prekṣya bhīmaṃ tathāgatam saṃkruddho rākṣaso ghoras tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, O king, seeing Bhīma in such a plight, that dreadful Rākṣasa, filled with wrath, vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā dāruṇāṃ māyāṃ bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinīm adṛśyata nimeṣārdhād ghorarūpaṃ samāśritaḥ
english: Weaving a terrible illusion that swelled the fear of the timid, in half the blink of an eye he reappeared, clad in a fearsome form.

sanskrit: airāvataṃ samāruhya svayaṃ māyāmayaṃ kṛtam tasya cānye 'pi diṅnāgā babhūvur anuyāyinaḥ
english: He himself mounted Airāvata, conjured by his magic, and other elephants of the quarters became his followers as well.

sanskrit: añjano vāmanaś caiva mahāpadmaś ca suprabhaḥ traya ete mahānāgā rākṣasaiḥ samadhiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Añjana, Vāmana, and resplendent Mahāpadma—these three great elephants were ridden by Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mahākāyās tridhā rājan prasravanto madaṃ bahu tejovīryabalopetā mahābalaparākramāḥ
english: Of vast bulk, O king, streaming rut in three currents, endowed with splendor, vigor, and strength, mighty in might and prowess.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tu svaṃ nāgaṃ codayām āsa taṃ tataḥ sagajaṃ bhagadattaṃ tu hantukāmaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, that scorcher of foes, urged on his own elephant, eager to slay Bhagadatta together with his mount.

sanskrit: te cānye coditā nāgā rākṣasais tair mahābalaiḥ paripetuḥ susaṃrabdhāś caturdaṃṣṭrāś caturdiśam bhagadattasya taṃ nāgaṃ viṣāṇais te 'bhyapīḍayan
english: And those other elephants, driven on by the mighty Rākṣasas, four-tusked and furious, fell upon Bhagadatta's elephant from the four quarters and gored it with their tusks.

sanskrit: saṃpīḍyamānas tair nāgair vedanārtaḥ śarāturaḥ so 'nadat sumahānādam indrāśanisamasvanam
english: Crushed by those elephants, anguished with pain and tormented by arrows, it bellowed a tremendous cry, loud as the thunderbolt of Indra.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ nadato nādaṃ sughoraṃ bhīmanisvanam śrutvā bhīṣmo 'bravīd droṇaṃ rājānaṃ ca suyodhanam
english: Hearing that frightful, terrible-sounding cry of the bellowing beast, Bhīṣma spoke to Droṇa and to King Suyodhana:

sanskrit: eṣa yudhyati saṃgrāme haiḍimbena durātmanā bhagadatto maheṣvāsaḥ kṛcchreṇa parivartate
english: "Yonder Bhagadatta, the great archer, fights in battle with the wicked son of Hiḍimbā, and contends only with great difficulty."

sanskrit: rākṣasaś ca mahāmāyaḥ sa ca rājātikopanaḥ tau sametau mahāvīryau kālamṛtyusamāv ubhau
english: "The Rākṣasa is a master of illusion, and the king is exceedingly wrathful—the two have met, both of great valor, both like Time and Death itself."

sanskrit: śrūyate hy eṣa hṛṣṭānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāsvanaḥ hastinaś caiva sumahān bhītasya ruvato dhvaniḥ
english: "Here is heard the great clamor of the exultant Pāṇḍavas, and the mighty cry of the elephant trumpeting in its terror."

sanskrit: tatra gacchāma bhadraṃ vo rājānaṃ parirakṣitum arakṣyamāṇaḥ samare kṣipraṃ prāṇān vimokṣyate
english: "Let us go there—good fortune to you—to guard the king; unguarded in the fray, he will swiftly yield up his life."

sanskrit: te tvaradhvaṃ mahāvīryāḥ kiṃ cireṇa prayāmahe mahān hi vartate raudraḥ saṃgrāmo lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: "Make haste, O heroes of great valor! Why should we tarry to set out? For a great and dreadful battle rages on, one to make the hair stand on end."

sanskrit: bhaktaś ca kulaputraś ca śūraś ca pṛtanāpatiḥ yuktaṃ tasya paritrāṇaṃ kartum asmābhir acyutāḥ
english: "Devoted, nobly born, valiant, a leader of armies is he—it is fitting, O unfaltering ones, that we should make his rescue."

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya tad vacaḥ śrutvā bhāradvājapurogamāḥ sahitāḥ sarvarājāno bhagadattaparīpsayā uttamaṃ javam āsthāya prayayur yatra so 'bhavat
english: Hearing those words of Bhīṣma, all the kings together, led by the son of Bharadvāja, desiring to save Bhagadatta, set out at top speed to where he was.

sanskrit: tān prayātān samālokya yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayuḥ parān
english: Marking them depart, the Pāñcālas, led by Yudhiṣṭhira and joined by the Pāṇḍavas, followed the foe from behind.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāny athālokya rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān nanāda sumahānādaṃ visphoṭam aśaner iva
english: Then, beholding those armies, the valiant lord of the Rākṣasas roared a mighty roar, like the bursting crash of a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ ninadaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā nāgāṃś ca yudhyataḥ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo bhūyo bhāradvājam abhāṣata
english: Hearing that din of his and seeing the elephants doing battle, Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, spoke once more to the son of Bharadvāja:

sanskrit: na rocate me saṃgrāmo haiḍimbena durātmanā balavīryasamāviṣṭaḥ sasahāyaś ca sāṃpratam
english: "This battle with the wicked son of Hiḍimbā does not please me; for now he is filled with strength and valor, and has allies besides."

sanskrit: naiṣa śakyo yudhā jetum api vajrabhṛtā svayam labdhalakṣyaḥ prahārī ca vayaṃ ca śrāntavāhanāḥ pāñcālaiḥ pāṇḍaveyaiś ca divasaṃ kṣatavikṣatāḥ
english: "He cannot be vanquished in fight, not even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself; he is a sure-aiming smiter, while our mounts are weary and we are gashed and torn all day long by the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: tan na me rocate yuddhaṃ pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ ghuṣyatām avahāro 'dya śvo yotsyāmaḥ paraiḥ saha
english: "Therefore this battle with the triumphant Pāṇḍavas does not please me. Let the withdrawal be proclaimed for today; tomorrow we shall fight with the foe."

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā tathā cakruḥ sma kauravāḥ upāyenāpayānaṃ te ghaṭotkacabhayārditāḥ
english: Hearing the words of the grandsire, the Kauravas did accordingly; tormented by fear of Ghaṭotkaca, they contrived their retreat by stratagem.

sanskrit: kauraveṣu nivṛtteṣu pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ siṃhanādam akurvanta śaṅkhaveṇusvanaiḥ saha
english: When the Kauravas had turned back, the victorious Pāṇḍavas raised a lion's roar, mingled with the blare of conches and the sound of flutes.

sanskrit: evaṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ divasaṃ bharatarṣabha pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca puraskṛtya ghaṭotkacam
english: Thus, O bull of the Bhāratas, did the day's battle between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus unfold, with Ghaṭotkaca set in the forefront.

sanskrit: kauravās tu tato rājan prayayuḥ śibiraṃ svakam vrīḍamānā niśākāle pāṇḍaveyaiḥ parājitāḥ
english: Then the Kauravas, O king, set out for their own camp, abashed at nightfall, defeated by the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: śaravikṣatagātrāś ca pāṇḍuputrā mahārathāḥ yuddhe sumanaso bhūtvā śibirāyaiva jagmire
english: The sons of Pāṇḍu too, those great car-warriors, their bodies torn by arrows, glad of heart from the battle, made their way to their camp.

sanskrit: puraskṛtya mahārāja bhīmasenaghaṭotkacau pūjayantas tadānyonyaṃ mudā paramayā yutāḥ
english: Setting Bhīmasena and Ghaṭotkaca at their head, O great king, they honored one another, filled with the highest joy.

sanskrit: nadanto vividhān nādāṃs tūryasvanavimiśritān siṃhanādāṃś ca kurvāṇā vimiśrāñ śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ
english: Sounding manifold cries mingled with the blare of trumpets, and raising lion-roars blended with the notes of conches,

sanskrit: vinadanto mahātmānaḥ kampayantaś ca medinīm ghaṭṭayantaś ca marmāṇi tava putrasya māriṣa prayātāḥ śibirāyaiva niśākāle paraṃtapāḥ
english: those great-souled ones, roaring aloud and making the earth tremble, striking at the very heart of your son, O sire—those scorchers of foes set out for their camp at nightfall.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu nṛpatir dīno bhrātṛvadhena ca muhūrtaṃ cintayām āsa bāṣpaśokasamākulaḥ
english: But King Duryodhana, dejected at the slaying of his brothers, brooded for a while, overcome by tears and grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtvā vidhiṃ sarvaṃ śibirasya yathāvidhi pradadhyau śokasaṃtapto bhrātṛvyasanakarśitaḥ
english: Then, having made all due arrangements for the camp according to custom, he sat sunk in thought, consumed by sorrow and worn by the calamity that had befallen his brothers.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhayaṃ me sumahaj jātaṃ vismayaś caiva saṃjaya śrutvā pāṇḍukumārāṇāṃ karma devaiḥ suduṣkaram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A great fear has come upon me, Saṃjaya, and amazement too, on hearing of the deeds of the sons of Pāṇḍu, deeds hard even for the gods to perform.

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ ca parābhavaṃ śrutvā saṃjaya sarvaśaḥ cintā me mahatī sūta bhaviṣyati kathaṃ tv iti
english: And hearing, Saṃjaya, of the utter defeat of my sons, great is my anxiety, O charioteer: how, in the end, shall it be?

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ viduravākyāni dhakṣyanti hṛdayaṃ mama yathā hi dṛśyate sarvaṃ daivayogena saṃjaya
english: Surely the words of Vidura shall sear my heart, for all unfolds, it seems, by the working of fate, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yatra bhīṣmamukhāñ śūrān astrajñān yodhasattamān pāṇḍavānām anīkāni yodhayanti prahāriṇaḥ
english: —seeing that the smiting hosts of the Pāṇḍavas do battle against heroes led by Bhīṣma, masters of weapons, the very best of warriors.

sanskrit: kenāvadhyā mahātmānaḥ pāṇḍuputrā mahābalāḥ kena dattavarās tāta kiṃ vā jñānaṃ vidanti te yena kṣayaṃ na gacchanti divi tārāgaṇā iva
english: By whom are the great-souled, mighty sons of Pāṇḍu made invincible? By whom were they granted boons, my son, or what knowledge do they possess, that they perish not, like the hosts of stars in heaven?

sanskrit: punaḥ punar na mṛṣyāmi hataṃ sainyaṃ sma pāṇḍavaiḥ mayy eva daṇḍaḥ patati daivāt paramadāruṇaḥ
english: Again and again I cannot bear it—my army slaughtered by the Pāṇḍavas. It is upon me alone that the rod of fate falls, most terrible of all.

sanskrit: yathāvadhyāḥ pāṇḍusutā yathā vadhyāś ca me sutāḥ etan me sarvam ācakṣva yathātattvena saṃjaya
english: How it is that the sons of Pāṇḍu cannot be slain, and how my sons are doomed to die—all this declare to me truly, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: na hi pāraṃ prapaśyāmi duḥkhasyāsya kathaṃ cana samudrasyeva mahato bhujābhyāṃ prataran naraḥ
english: For I can see no farther shore of this sorrow by any means, like a man striving to swim across the mighty ocean with his arms.

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ vyasanaṃ manye dhruvaṃ prāptaṃ sudāruṇam ghātayiṣyati me putrān sarvān bhīmo na saṃśayaḥ
english: I deem that a most dreadful calamity has surely come upon my sons; Bhīma will cause them all to be slain—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi taṃ vīraṃ yo me rakṣet sutān raṇe dhruvaṃ vināśaḥ samare putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya
english: For I see no hero who might guard my sons in battle; certain is the destruction of my sons in the fray, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: tasmān me kāraṇaṃ sūta yuktiṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ pṛcchato 'dya yathātattvaṃ sarvam ākhyātum arhasi
english: Therefore, O charioteer, as I ask you now, you must tell me truly everything—the cause and, above all, the reason of it.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi yac cakre dṛṣṭvā svān vimukhān raṇe bhīṣmadroṇau kṛpaś caiva saubaleyo jayadrathaḥ drauṇir vāpi maheṣvāso vikarṇo vā mahābalaḥ
english: And what Duryodhana did on seeing his own men turn their backs in battle—Bhīṣma and Droṇa, and Kṛpa, and the son of Subala, and Jayadratha, or the great archer Aśvatthāman, or the mighty Vikarṇa—

sanskrit: niścayo vāpi kas teṣāṃ tadā hy āsīn mahātmanām vimukheṣu mahāprājña mama putreṣu saṃjaya
english: —and what resolve was then taken by those great-souled ones when my sons turned away, O most wise Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahitaḥ śrutvā caivāvadhāraya naiva mantrakṛtaṃ kiṃ cin naiva māyāṃ tathāvidhām na vai vibhīṣikāṃ kāṃ cid rājan kurvanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Listen attentively, O king, and having heard, take it to heart. No spell-craft of any kind, no such illusion, and no terrifying trickery, O king, do the Pāṇḍavas employ.

sanskrit: yudhyanti te yathānyāyaṃ śaktimantaś ca saṃyuge dharmeṇa sarvakāryāṇi kīrtitānīti bhārata ārabhante sadā pārthāḥ prārthayānā mahad yaśaḥ
english: They fight as is just, and they are mighty in the field. Holding that all their deeds are renowned through righteousness, O Bhārata, the sons of Pṛthā ever undertake them, seeking great glory.

sanskrit: na te yuddhān nivartante dharmopetā mahābalāḥ śriyā paramayā yuktā yato dharmas tato jayaḥ tenāvadhyā raṇe pārthā jayayuktāś ca pārthiva
english: They turn not back from battle, those mighty ones endowed with righteousness and joined to surpassing fortune; where there is righteousness, there is victory. For this the sons of Pṛthā are unslayable in war and ever victorious, O king.

sanskrit: tava putrā durātmānaḥ pāpeṣv abhiratāḥ sadā niṣṭhurā hīnakarmāṇas tena hīyanti saṃyuge
english: Your sons are evil-souled, ever delighting in sins, cruel, and base in their deeds; for this they come to grief in battle.

sanskrit: subahūni nṛśaṃsāni putrais tava janeśvara nikṛtānīha pāṇḍūnāṃ nīcair iva yathā naraiḥ
english: Very many cruel wrongs were done by your sons here against the sons of Pāṇḍu, O lord of men, as if by men of the lowest sort.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ ca tad anādṛtya putrāṇāṃ tava kilbiṣam sāpahnavāḥ sadaivāsan pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja na cainān bahu manyante putrās tava viśāṃ pate
english: Yet disregarding all those offenses of your sons, the Pāṇḍavas were ever forbearing, O elder of the Pāṇḍu line; but your sons hold them in no esteem, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tasya pāpasya satataṃ kriyamāṇasya karmaṇaḥ saṃprāptaṃ sumahad ghoraṃ phalaṃ kiṃpākasaṃnibham sa tad bhuṅkṣva mahārāja saputraḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
english: Of that evil deed done ceaselessly there has now come a great and terrible fruit, like the fruit of the kiṃpāka. Devour it, O great king, together with your sons and your friends.

sanskrit: nāvabudhyasi yad rājan vāryamāṇaḥ suhṛjjanaiḥ vidureṇātha bhīṣmeṇa droṇena ca mahātmanā
english: You would not heed, O king, though restrained by your well-wishers—by Vidura, and Bhīṣma, and the great-souled Droṇa—

sanskrit: tathā mayā cāpy asakṛd vāryamāṇo na gṛhṇasi vākyaṃ hitaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca martyaḥ pathyam ivauṣadham putrāṇāṃ matam āsthāya jitān manyasi pāṇḍavān
english: —and by me as well, restrained more than once. You took not the counsel both salutary and wholesome, as a dying man refuses the wholesome medicine; cleaving to your sons' opinion, you deemed the Pāṇḍavas already conquered.

sanskrit: śṛṇu bhūyo yathātattvaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi kāraṇaṃ bharataśreṣṭha pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaṃ prati tat te 'haṃ kathayiṣyāmi yathāśrutam ariṃdama
english: Hear now once more, truly, that of which you ask me—the cause of the Pāṇḍavas' victory, O best of the Bhāratas. That will I tell you as I have heard it, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: duryodhanena saṃpṛṣṭa etam arthaṃ pitāmahaḥ dṛṣṭvā bhrātṝn raṇe sarvān nirjitān sumahārathān
english: Questioned by Duryodhana on this matter, the grandsire—having seen all his brothers, mighty car-warriors, vanquished in battle—

sanskrit: śokasaṃmūḍhahṛdayo niśākāle sma kauravaḥ pitāmahaṃ mahāprājñaṃ vinayenopagamya ha yad abravīt sutas te 'sau tan me śṛṇu janeśvara
english: —that scion of Kuru, his heart bewildered with grief, approaching the most wise grandsire with humility at nightfall—what your son then said, hear it from me, O lord of men.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca tvaṃ ca droṇaś ca śalyaś ca kṛpo drauṇis tathaiva ca kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyaḥ kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: You, and Droṇa, and Śalya, and Kṛpa, and likewise the son of Droṇa, and Kṛtavarman the son of Hṛdika, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja,

sanskrit: bhūriśravā vikarṇaś ca bhagadattaś ca vīryavān mahārathāḥ samākhyātāḥ kulaputrās tanutyajaḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, and Vikarṇa, and the valiant Bhagadatta—you are all famed as great car-warriors, nobly born, ready to lay down your lives.

sanskrit: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ paryāptā iti me matiḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ samastāś ca na tiṣṭhanti parākrame
english: To my mind you are a match even for the three worlds; yet against the prowess of the Pāṇḍavas you all cannot stand.

sanskrit: tatra me saṃśayo jātas tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ yaṃ samāśritya kaunteyā jayanty asmān pade pade
english: Herein a doubt has arisen in me; declare it to me as I ask—on whom do the sons of Kuntī rely, that they conquer us at every step?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājan vaco mahyaṃ yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi kaurava bahuśaś ca mamokto 'si na ca me tattvayā kṛtam
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear my word, O king, which I shall speak to you, O scion of Kuru. Often have I told you this, yet you have not acted upon it.

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ śamo bharatasattama etat kṣamam ahaṃ manye pṛthivyās tava cābhibho
english: Let peace be made with the Pāṇḍavas, O best of the Bhāratas; this I deem fitting, for the earth's sake and for your own, O lord.

sanskrit: bhuñjemāṃ pṛthivīṃ rājan bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sukhī durhṛdas tāpayan sarvān nandayaṃś cāpi bāndhavān
english: Enjoy this earth, O king, in happiness together with your brothers, scorching all your enemies and gladdening your kinsmen too.

sanskrit: na ca me krośatas tāta śrutavān asi vai purā tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ yat pāṇḍūn avamanyase
english: You would not listen to me of old, my son, though I cried out; and now this has come upon you, because you scorned the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: yaś ca hetur avadhyatve teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām taṃ śṛṇuṣva mahārāja mama kīrtayataḥ prabho
english: And what the cause is of the invincibility of those whose deeds are untiring—hear it, O great king, as I declare it, O lord.
